items.title: JAX v0.12.0
items.abstract_or_text: * New features * Added `jax.scipy.special.erfcinv` for the inverse complementary error function. * Added `jax.lax.polynomial` for polynomial evaluation. The polynomial primitive is faster and uses less memory when computing gradients. * Added `jax.custom_vjp.defremat`, which customizes how a `jax.custom_vjp` function is rematerialized when it's differentiated under `jax.remat`. It requires the `jax_custom_vjp3` and `jax_remat3` implementations. * Added a `remat` option to `jax.custom_gradient`, for writing `jax.custom_vjp.defremat` rules with closures. * `arr.at[...].get()` now accepts a `strategy` argument that allows choosing whether the operation lowers to `gather`, `dynamic_slice`, or `slice`. * Added a `generic_batching` option to `jax.custom_vjp.defvjp`, for batching under `jax.vmap` when a primal output is shared across the batch. See `jax-301-vmap-shared-outputs`. * `jax.nn.get_scaled_dot_general_config` accepts `'mxfp4'`: E2M1 elements with one E8M0 scale per block of 32, for `jax.nn.scaled_dot_general`. The quantization is executed natively on AMD gfx950 GPUs and by a dequantize-and-dot fallback elsewhere. * JAX now registers a `proxy` backend, which connects to an IFRT Proxy server such as [Pathways on Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/ai-hypercomputer/docs/workloads/pathways-on-cloud/pathways-intro). To use it, set `JAX_PLATFORMS=proxy` and set `JAX_BACKEND_TARGET` to the server address, e.g. `grpc://localhost:29000`. * Added `jax.sharding.no_collectives`, a context manager that raises an error at trace time in explicit sharding mode if an operation or `jax.sharding.reshard` introduces a collective across any specified mesh axis. * Added `jax.custom_vjp.defremat_with_logs`, allowing `jax.custom_vjp.defremat` rules (and `jax.custom_gradient` with `remat=True` and `with_logs=True`) to log values from the backward pass (#40956). * `jax.scipy.linalg.eigh` now supports generalized Hermitian eigenproblems (`b != None`) for problem types `type=1`, `2`, and `3` (#41162, #41197). * Added `jax.profiler.ProfileSession` and `jax.profiler.export_profile_data` for session- and context-manager-based profiling. * Added `jax.experimental.layout.Layout.for_array` to query the default device layout for an array. * Added a `strict_in_out` argument to `jax.experimental.program_order` to place optimization barriers on the first input and/or last output of the scope. * Added `jax.experimental.thunky` for authoring, inspecting, splicing, and executing XLA:GPU `ThunkExecutor` programs directly from Python. * Added JVP rule for `jax.lax.nextafter`, enabling forward- and reverse-mode autodiff through `nextafter` (#38679). * Widened `jax.random.ball`'s `p` parameter type from `float` to `RealArray`, allowing array-valued norm orders (#41546). * Added support for DLPack 1.0 (`DLManagedTensorVersioned`) and read-only DLPack tensors (#40789). * [oneAPI GPU] Added SYCL/oneMKL kernels for `jax.lax.linalg.lu_pivots_to_permutation`, `jax.lax.linalg.cholesky_update`, `jax.lax.linalg.tridiagonal_solve` (with `perturb_singular=True`), `jax.lax.linalg.tridiagonal` (`sytrd`/`hetrd`), symmetric rank-k updates (`syrk`), and `scaled_matmul`, and set `jax_oneapi_visible_devices` in `jax.distributed.initialize`. * [ROCm] Added `gfx1250` to the default target architectures in ROCm builds (#40877). * Breaking changes * Removed `jax.custom_remat`. Use `jax.custom_vjp.defremat` instead: `custom_remat(f, f_fwd, f_rem, f_bwd)` becomes `f = jax.custom_vjp(f)` followed by `f.defremat(f_fwd, f_rem, f_bwd)`. * On x86-64, JAX and `jaxlib` now require an Intel Haswell or newer CPU (roughly 2013 onwards, requiring AVX2 and FMA support). Older CPUs that only support AVX are no longer supported, though you can still build from source for older CPUs. * `jax.numpy.atleast_1d`, `jax.numpy.atleast_2d`, and `jax.numpy.atleast_3d` now return tuples of arrays rather than lists, matching the behavior in NumPy 2.0+. * The `shape` argument of `jax.random.multinomial` is now the batch shape, as documented and as in NumPy: the result has shape `(*shape, p.shape[-1])`. Previously `shape` had to include the outcome axis. Code that passed the full output shape should drop its last entry. * Under `jax.vmap`, a `jax.custom_vjp` function with a primal output that doesn't depend on any batched input could get gradients that counted that output's cotangent once per example. That case now raises an error explaining how to resolve it, for example with the new `generic_batching` option. See `jax-301-vmap-shared-outputs`. * Dropped support for NumPy 2.1; JAX now requires NumPy 2.2 or newer. * `jax.numpy.cross` no longer accepts 2D vector inputs, completing a deprecation started in JAX 0.11.0 (#40876). * The `copy`, `order`, and `ndmin` arguments to `jax.numpy.array` are now keyword-only, completing a deprecation started in an earlier release (#40878). * `jax.profiler.ProfileOptions` now raises `AttributeError` when unknown attributes are assigned to it. * `jax.checkpoint`, `jax.custom_vjp`, and `jax.shard_map` now raise an error if the same `Ref` is passed as more than one argument or is both closed over and passed as an argument. * Deprecations * `jax.lax.psend` and `jax.lax.precv` are deprecated. * Changes * Improved the numerical accuracy of `jax.scipy.special.ndtri` and its derivatives by replacing the piecewise rational approximations with minimax polynomial approximations and a custom JVP rule. * JAX now uses Bazel 9.2.0 to build from source. * Improved the numerical accuracy of complex `jax.numpy.abs` and `jax.lax.abs` by lowering through power-of-two scaled `hypot`. * Improved the numerical accuracy of `jax.numpy.hypot` and its derivatives by replacing the division-based formula with power-of-two scaling and a custom JVP rule, avoiding rounding errors for large inputs. The derivative at `(0, 0)` now returns `NaN` (previously `±0.5`). * Improved the numerical accuracy of `jax.numpy.sinc` across all floating-point types (to \le 0.5 ULP for `bfloat16` and `float16`, \le 2.5–4.0 ULPs for `float32`, and \ge 2.0 ULPs for `float64`). * `jax.numpy.ldexp` and `jax.numpy.frexp` are now bit-exact for normal floating-point numbers, replacing floating-point arithmetic with bitwise operations. Subnormal inputs and underflowing outputs are flushed to signed zero. * Several `jax.numpy` functions are now implemented in terms of HiJax primitives (see `jax-301-hijax-types`). This includes `~jax.numpy.searchsorted`, `~jax.numpy.nonzero`, `~jax.numpy.ldexp`, `jax.numpy.frexp`. Typical users should not see any change in behavior, but you may notice more efficient batching and autodiff, and more concise representations in jaxprs. * The "web" debugger now defaults to hostname "localhost", which is a safer default that avoids inadvertently opening a port to the world. * `jax.numpy.lexsort` with many keys now uses a batched approach by default, controlled by the new `batch_size` parameter (which defaults to 16). This avoids long compile times for sorts with many keys. Fixes the poor performance of `jax.numpy.unique` for high-dimensional arrays (#17370). * Reimplemented `jax.scipy.special.erfcx` and added `accuracy=jax.lax.AccuracyMode.HIGHEST` support for `jax.lax.erfc`, improving worst-case `float32` accuracy to \le 3.5–5.5 ULPs across CPU, GPU, and TPU (and \le 2.5–3.0 ULPs in `float64`) with accurate first- and higher-order derivatives. * Improved `float32` accuracy of `jax.lax.lgamma` (`jax.scipy.special.gammaln`) to \le 4 ULPs across CPU, GPU, and TPU (#21284). * Improved `float32` and `float64` accuracy of `jax.lax.expm1` on CPU to = 0.0.50`). * Improved precision of `jax.lax.asin` fallback expansions near zero under flush-to-zero mode. * `jax.scipy.special.betainc` now stops its continued fraction iteration per element as each element converges rather than running until all batch elements converge (#28547). * `jax.pure_callback` and `jax.experimental.io_callback` now clear the caller's concrete and abstract mesh when invoking host callbacks, matching `jax.debug.callback`. * `jax.numpy.quantile` and `jax.numpy.percentile` now use an unstable sort when `weights=None`, avoiding a companion index sort. * `jax.numpy.minmax` now lowers via a single-pass `jax.lax.reduce`. * Implemented `__reversed__` on `jax.Array` using chunked slicing, matching `__iter__` for faster reverse iteration in eager mode. * Updated minimum pinned `libtpu` version to `0.0.50`. * When cache key equality comparison fails in `weakref_lru_cache`, JAX now raises a descriptive `ValueError` reporting the non-comparable key types (#21825). * Type annotation improvements * `jax.numpy.int32`, `jax.numpy.float32`, and other scalar constructors now have proper type annotations; prior to v0.12.0 they were typed `Any`. This may lead to new typecheck errors in cases where they were being misused; for example, if they were assumed to be instances of `jnp.dtype` (which they are not) or used as annotations for arrays of a given type (which is invalid). * `jax.Array.__iter__` and `jax.Array.__reversed__` are now annotated as returning `Iterator[Self]` rather than `Any`. * `jax.random.Key` was introduced as an `Array` type alias. Starting in JAX v0.13.0, this will be the return type for `jax.random.key`, `jax.random.split`, and `jax.random.fold_in`. * Unary `jax.Array` methods, `jax.Array.astype`, and `arr.at[...].set()` now use `Self` return type annotations (#41055, #41324). * Bug fixes * Fixed the gradient of `jax.numpy.ldexp` at `x = 0.0`, which previously returned `1.0` instead of `2**n`. * `jax.nn.scaled_dot_general` keeps its FP8/FP4 quantization when XLA expands the scaled matmul into a dequantize-and-dot (previously the rounding could be folded away under `xla_allow_excess_precision`) and computes MX block scales in float32 regardless of the input dtype. * Fixed the derivative of `jax.lax.sign` and `jax.numpy.sign` for complex inputs, which was previously always zero (`#41000`). * `jax.scipy.linalg.lu` now accepts batched inputs of shape `(..., M, N)`, as documented; previously it raised a `ValueError` for any input with more than two dimensions. * Fixed reverse-mode autodiff for `jax.experimental.sparse.coo_matvec`, `jax.experimental.sparse.coo_matmat`, `jax.experimental.sparse.csr_matvec`, and `jax.experimental.sparse.csr_matmat` when `transpose=True` (#40625). * Fixed `jax.numpy.linalg.svd` with `hermitian=True` breaking unitarity when a singular value is zero (#41547). * Fixed gradient cancellation in `jax.lax.expm1`, `jax.nn.elu`, and `jax.nn.selu` for large negative inputs (#39794, #39795, #39796). * Fixed numerical overflow in `jax.lax.asinh` gradients for large inputs. * Fixed precision, overflow, and `NaN`/`inf` handling in `jax.scipy.special.rel_entr` and `jax.scipy.special.kl_div` (#38239, #38262, #41200). * Fixed domain, boundary, and overflow issues in `jax.scipy.special.expn` and `jax.scipy.special.expi` at `x = 0` (#41221). * Fixed `jax.scipy.special.betaln` Hessian when `a == b`. * Fixed `jax.scipy.special.zeta`'s JVP rule returning finite primal values outside its domain (`x < 1`) where `zeta` returns `NaN` (#40968). * Fixed `jax.scipy.stats.norm.isf` losing precision and returning `inf` for small tail probabilities (#41262). * Fixed `jax.scipy.stats.expon.logcdf` returning `-inf` for small positive inputs (#40965). * Fixed `NaN` gradients in `jax.scipy.stats.laplace.cdf` in the tails (#40966) and in `jax.scipy.stats.poisson.entropy` (#40969). * Fixed domain handling and tail accuracy in `jax.scipy.stats.cauchy.ppf` and `jax.scipy.stats.cauchy.isf` (#38318). * Fixed `jax.scipy.stats.vonmises.logpdf` at `kappa = 0` (#38621) and `jax.scipy.stats.chi2.logpdf` at `x = 0` and `x = inf` for `df = 2` (#38316). * Fixed `jax.scipy.stats.multinomial.logpmf` and `pmf` for batched `x` and `n` (#38605), `jax.scipy.stats.poisson.logpmf` for fractional `loc` (#41220), `jax.scipy.stats.pareto` support checks when `scale` is below the floating-point resolution of `loc` (#40964), and `NaN` propagation in `jax.scipy.stats.uniform` and `jax.scipy.stats.truncnorm` (#38317, #38606). * Fixed parameter broadcasting in `jax.random.f`. * Fixed `jax.Array.sum` to forward the `initial` parameter to `jax.numpy.sum` (#41137). * Fixed `jax.numpy.ufunc.reduceat` ignoring the specified `dtype` when casting inputs before accumulation (#41247). * Fixed `jax.numpy.partition`, `jax.numpy.argpartition`, and `jax.lax.top_k` returning incorrect results for signed integer minimum values (e.g. `INT_MIN`). * Fixed transpose rule for `jax.lax.select_n` with out-of-range integer indices or a single case (#10993). * Propagated `mode`, `indices_are_sorted`, and `unique_indices` through `jax.lax.scatter_max` and `jax.lax.scatter_min` JVP rules (#40626). * Fixed input shape validation in `jax.numpy.linalg.eigh`, `jax.scipy.linalg.eigh`, and `jax.numpy.linalg.cholesky`, and raised `NotImplementedError` for unimplemented JVP of `jax.lax.linalg.svd` with partial `subset_by_index` and `compute_uv=True` (#41210). * Fixed handling of negative `static_argnums` and `donate_argnums` with named parameters in `jax.jit` (#40988), and fixed keyword argument forwarding in `jax.fwd_and_bwd` (#41156). * Fixed indexing and iteration over fully replicated multi-device arrays and out-of-bounds slice validation when `start = 0`. * Fixed `jax.vmap` of `jax.lax.scan` closing over a `Ref` batched on a non-leading axis. * Fixed `jax.experimental.checkify` error code dtype mismatches under nested `jax.enable_x64()` scopes (#40482). * Fixed a regression where cached host-transfer CPU buffers prevented buffer donation, and prevented a failing ordered `io_callback` from permanently poisoning effect tokens.

It also fixes some other issues listed on the below commits. It contains the following commits: - Fix inputs dict casting in generate (#49731) by @Cyrilvallez - Fix zero expert gradients in bfloat16 with expert parallelism and ep_size < fsdp_size (#49688) by @qgallouedec - Declare the input modalities of the VLMs that report text only (#49677) by @qgallouedec - Avoid a host-to-device copy in eager_mask (#49684) by @hmellor

items.abstract_or_text: ui : Discover & Download Models from HF Hub (#29584) * common : resolve - download tags and list cached sidecars A Q4_0-mtp style tag now resolves the sidecar file when no model file matches it, so a solo draft or mmproj download actually pulls the file. Cached sidecar files list as their own entries so the state survives a restart, and removing such a tag deletes only the sidecar. Assisted-by: pi:zai-org/GLM-5.3 * ui : optional sanitized raw HTML in markdown Add an allowHtml prop to MarkdownContent: raw HTML found in the markdown is rendered after DOMPurify sanitization instead of being escaped as literal text. Default stays escaped. Assisted-by: pi:GLM-5.3-Flash * ui : add the discover models components The Discover surface: the curated-catalog list with its search and skeletons, the details pane with its readme, metadata, Hub stats and download options, and the standalone download progress bar that replaces the plain one. The quant download button sizes its select with a new xs trigger, so the select gains that size and the muted box look. The store stays incomplete when a repo fails, so the next mount retries it. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : put the discover view in the models manager The manager dialog gains its second view: the Discover Models call to action fades the table out, slides the title with its compass mark, and fades the discover surface in; the arrow button returns to the table. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash # Conflicts: # tools/ui/src/lib/components/ui/button/button.svelte * ui : add the Enable Discover Models setting The flag gates browsing and downloading HuggingFace GGUF models, so it is declared on the discover layer; the repo-tree lookup in the manager layer above reads it from here. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : resume model downloads from the pause point A stopped download keeps its partial file instead of deleting it, so re-posting the tag resumes from disk. The first progress record now carries the resume offset, the paused snapshot survives into the resumed entry, and a pause settles as soon as it is requested. Assisted-by: pi * ui : lead the discover list with downloads The discover sidebar lists running downloads above the suggested models, and steps aside while a query is active. A paused download stays in the manager table, where it is resumed or dropped. Assisted-by: pi * ui : make resuming a paused download work Re-posting the tag of a paused download hit the router's "already exists" check, because a paused download parks its entry as DOWNLOADED until the next reload: a download entry that is not running is now replaced and resumed. The UI keeps the paused row when the request still fails, instead of dropping it and looking finished. Assisted-by: pi * ui : remember unfinished model downloads A partial file is named after its content hash, so nothing on disk says which model it belongs to once the router restarts. The router now keeps the tags of the downloads it started, clears a tag when the download finishes or is deleted, and lists what is left as still downloading without starting anything. Assisted-by: pi * ui : collapse the download options by default The copyable download command starts collapsed so the option rows lead; expanding it stays one click away. Assisted-by: pi * common: settle sidecar names on the listing and drop unfinished partials An infix or trailing sidecar token is ambiguous: draft heads use it (Model-MTP-BF16.gguf), so do full models with embedded heads (Model-Q8D-MTP.gguf). Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * nit: Remove `+` before draft sidecar badge * server: list unfinished downloads as incomplete A download that never finished was reported as "downloading", the same status a live download carries, so a client could not tell a running download from a dead one. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * server: download a model with its sidecars as -hf does Resolution goes back to master. POST /models takes the sidecar kinds to pull with the model (mmproj by default) and the download child gets them as -hf flags, so the server picks the files. /models lists real models only, each with the sidecars it has on disk, and incomplete downloads keep their sidecars across restarts. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : keep the discover download list one row per model The list leads with one row per downloading model, its sidecars as sub-lines. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : carry the draft through the download options One chip per main quant, its draft badged on it and the chip's downloaded state covering both files. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * common : drop the partials of a removed sidecar Removing a sidecar alone left the .downloadInProgress files of the sidecars a download had planned in blobs/. The removal purges them through the same plan the download follows, and the test covers a finished draft beside an unfinished one, whose partial goes while the model keeps its files. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * server : name why a download is refused A model that is already downloading, or that is running, answered "already exists". It now says which: "is already downloading", or "is running, unload it first", both before the resumable check. The router test covers the two. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : post a download once per click Two quick clicks on the same chip posted twice, and the second answer was "already exists". The store tracks the model as pending, returns early while it is pending or in flight, and reads it as in flight before the server answers, so the chip shows the download at once. The new client test pins the flows: one POST per double click, the chip reading downloaded once the list reports the model, a resume keeping its sidecars, a cancel dropping the whole download, and a reload restoring the paused state. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : keep a plain download row the height of the others The sub-lines wrapper of a download row was rendered even with nothing in it, so its padding made the row taller than a plain one and the overlaid progress bar sat in that empty strip. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : badge a repo's draft once The args of a loaded model and the listing of a cached one report the same draft in different words, one with the file's quant and one with the kind alone, so the merge kept both and a repo row showed the same kind twice. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * server : report the sidecars of a preset or a download on its way A model the preset also names is registered as a preset, so its drafts were never reported and no row could badge them. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * common : report a removed sidecar that only had a partial Removing a sidecar alone dropped the result of the partial purge, so a sidecar that only ever landed as a .downloadInProgress blob answered false and the UI had no reason to refetch. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : ignore a pause while the download POST is still on its way The chip reads as downloading before the server answers, so a quick second click unloaded a model that had not started and left the store neither in flight nor paused. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : offer a missing draft as its own chip A model already on disk without its draft had no way to add it: the quant chip carried the draft, so it read as a download of both. The quant chip keeps to its own state now, its joined draft shows only while it rides along or is on disk, and a downloaded quant missing its draft gets a chip of its own - badge, size, download - that posts the model with that kind, so the server keeps the files already there and pulls the draft. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * server : list a paused sidecar download by the files on disk A model on disk whose sidecar download stops keeps its unfinished record, and the listing reported the kinds that record plans as if they were on disk: the UI checked a draft that never landed and offered no way to add it. The planned kinds now stand in only while the download runs. * chore: Clean up comments * server : list sidecars only for a model that resolves from a HF repo A preset on a local file has no HF repo, yet the listing resolved its name as one: the plan threw on the invalid repo format and GET /models failed for every model. The sidecars now come from the repo a preset names or a cached model is listed under, and a local file lists without them. * common : fix download cancel regression Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * common : preserve model partials when removing sidecars Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * server : one sidecar table and an unfinished downloads class Address review from @ggerganov. The sidecar kinds live in one table in common/download, mapping each name to its download option and plan file; the server validates, builds its options and lists cached sidecars through it instead of its own lists. The unfinished downloads move into server_unfinished_downloads, a record with its own mutex and a struct per entry, and server_models exposes them through unfinished_downloads_get and unfinished_downloads_remove. * common: one sidecar table, and removals that keep shared files The resolution, the cached listing and the removal follow a single table of sidecar kinds, so a kind is declared once with its file keyword, whether it is a draft, its option and its plan file. The server reads the same table for the kinds it accepts, the default sidecars and the child flags. Removing a tag keeps the files another cached tag still loads, such as an mmproj named after the removed quant. A sidecar removed on its own goes for every tag that resolves it. An unfinished download records the exact paths of its partials when it starts. A removal deletes those without asking the hub, and keeps a partial another recorded download also writes. The record is taken once the child is spawned, and the files go under the models lock, so a download of the same tag cannot start while they are removed. * server: drop stale partials and refuse a tag that resolves nothing Recording a download again deletes the partials of the earlier record that the new plan no longer writes, such as those of an older hub revision or of a sidecar the new request leaves out. A posted tag that resolves no file of the repo is refused before the download starts. Removing a model follows a single path, whether the reload erased its entry during the wait or not. * server: fix the CI race between the router download tests The pytest workers run in parallel on one shared cache, so a download test could find the file another test had just fetched and see no progress, or start from the unfinished downloads record another test wrote. Each download test now runs on an empty cache of its own. * server: refuse a DELETE of an unknown name and decide downloads in load() A DELETE of a name that is neither a model nor a recorded download went to common_download_remove, and without a tag it wiped the whole repo cache, including the files of a loaded quant or of a download on its way. Such a name is now not found, as it was before. A POST that downloads over an existing entry checked its state outside the lock, so a load of the same model in between got its instance killed. The checks now run in load(), under the lock, right before the spawn. The fake load time of the tests applies to model loads only, since a download worker loads none. * server: add incomplete_sidecars to the /models API A sidecar added to a cached model and then paused kept its record, but the listing showed only the complete model, so a fresh UI lost the pause. The model entry now carries incomplete_sidecars, the kinds its unfinished download has not written yet; a POST with the kind resumes one and a DELETE with it drops its partial. * common : drop a kept partial when a resume gets 416 Now that partials survive between attempts, an old or complete partial makes every retry fail with the same 416. Delete it so the next attempt can start over from zero. Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * common: drop a kept partial when a resume gets 200 A server that ignores the range answers 200 to a resume, and the kept partial then fails every attempt the same way a 416 does. Drop it as well, so the next attempt starts over without a range. * server: refuse a download that shares a partial with one on its way Two downloads of quants that share a file, the mmproj or an mtp picked by the closest bits, appended to the same partial and renamed a file with interleaved bytes. A download whose plan writes a partial that a running download also writes is now refused until that one is done. * common : check the saved etag before resuming a partial download Before resuming, compare the etag saved with the partial to the one the server now serves. If it is missing or different, start over, so a resumed download never mixes bytes from two versions of the file. items.abstract_or_text: tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table (#30674) * tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table Muse Spark makes test-llama-context fail on state_load, cp_h and cp_d on about six percent of the random seeds, with an NMSE of 1.0e-05 to 1.4e-05 against a threshold of 1.0e-05. The sliding window is what exposes it: a restored state keeps the window alone, so the attention of an SWA layer reduces over a different cell layout and the continuation is not bit exact. Every SWA model carries that, at 1e-08. Muse Spark carried it at 1e-05. The generator is what turns 1e-08 into 1e-05. A norm preserving residual gate holds alpha^2 + beta^2 == 1 and the conversion resolves both weights from one raw weight, while the generator draws every tensor on its own. The pair then scaled the stream and the branch independently, the stream lost an arbitrary factor at each layer, and the model became an amplifier. The weights the test ran on were not a Muse Spark. Per-tensor rules lived inside the write path, where a flag picked the values of a tensor inside each of the two branches that store them, so a new rule meant a new flag threaded through both. The file asks to be rid of that in a TODO of its own. Give each rule a filler, pick one from a table keyed on a substring of the tensor name, and keep a single write path behind it. Mamba moves into the table and Muse Spark joins it: the gate filler draws the raw weight once per block and resolves alpha and beta the way the conversion does. Over a thousand seeds on a CPU build the worst case drops from 1.36e-05 to 2.48e-06 and the median from 4.10e-06 to 5.48e-07, with no seed above the threshold. The other 131 models come out identical to the bit, since no other architecture carries these tensors. ctest is green on a CPU build and on a CUDA build. * tests: draw every tensor filler from fill_normal The fillers repeated the generator and the distribution each time. The normal draw now takes its key and the other fillers transform its values, so the generator lives in one place. The generated models are identical to the bit. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11712/llama-b11712-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support (#30673) * model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support Kolibri-1 is a bilingual German/English MoE reasoning model with 78B parameters and 3.46B active per token: 50 layers, 384 routed experts plus one shared expert. Attention interleaves four sliding layers at a 513 window with one full layer. The sliding layers rotate with NeoX RoPE, the full layers are NoPE. GQA runs 48 query heads against 4 KV heads at head_dim 128 with a QK-RMSNorm, and every block carries four RMSNorms, so the attention and the MLP output are normalized before they rejoin the residual stream. Routing picks the experts from logits + expert_bias and weights them with the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, without renorm. The converter reuses AfmoeModel for the per-expert checkpoint layout and the expert selection bias, and writes the shared expert and the per layer sliding window pattern. The released FP8 checkpoint needs no special code, it goes through the generic weight_scale_inv path. Three tensor names are added to the mapping (post_attn_norm, post_ffn_norm, moe.router.expert_bias) and the 128k vocabulary registers the qwen2 pre-tokenizer by hash. The arch is registered in test-llama-archs, with GQA and the sliding window pattern. items.abstract_or_text: hexagon: vectorize softplus with HVX (#30435) softplus_f32 and tile_softplus_f32 ran a scalar logf(1.0f + expf(x)) loop. Replace both with a shared hvx_softplus_f32_aa() helper built from the backend's existing hvx_vec_exp_f32 / hvx_vec_log_f32 primitives, so no new numerical approximation is introduced. hvx_vec_exp_f32 clamps its input to (-88, 88) before exponentiating, so a naive log(1 + exp(x)) composition would saturate to ~88.72 for large x instead of returning x. The Q6_V_vmux_QVV select keeps the scalar reference's x > 20 guard (ggml_compute_softplus_f32 in ggml-impl.h), which is what makes the vector path match the CPU result.
